countryExplainByClass.managed: The official rate is what banks and governments quote. In {country} banks sell few dollars, so people buy them from each other and pay {street_price} {currency} where the official rate says {official_rate}.
countryExplainByClass.market: The official rate is what banks and governments quote. In {country} that rate follows the market, but people buying a dollar from each other pay {street_price} {currency} where it says {official_rate}.
countryExplainByClass.pegged: The official rate is what banks and governments quote. In {country} the currency is fixed to the dollar, so the gap is mostly what it costs to buy a stablecoin. People pay {street_price} {currency} where the official rate says {official_rate}.
countryExplainByClass.unmaintained: The official rate is what banks and governments quote. In {country} that rate has stopped being updated, so the gap is not a fair comparison. People pay {street_price} {currency} where the old rate says {official_rate}.
countryExplainByClass.default: The official rate is what banks and governments quote. In {country} people pay {street_price} {currency} for a dollar where the official rate says {official_rate}.
